thread:
maria: heads-up — saw a sustained p99 spike on model-x at ~6000 r/s starting ~02:12 UTC. baseline p99 was ~120ms, jumped to 420-600ms intermittently after ~2h. correlates with KV cache pressure and frequent evictions.
aj: looking. are these requests with long seq lengths or lots of unique prefixes? any recent rollout?
maria: mostly short chats (<=128 tokens) but high cardinality of prefixes. no rollout in that window. memory_iostat shows KV eviction count rising steeply.
sam: quick profiler dump shows microbatching windows expanding under contention — MB builder waits longer because KV lookups blocked on eviction. pushing MB size up gave throughput but worsened tail.
jia: that matches a kernel-selection edge case I patched last month — when seq_len < 64 we use kernel-A (fast) but on KV-miss path we do an extra memcpy + serialize which bumps latency. under heavy eviction threads stall doing KV rehydration.
maria: attaching small log excerpt:```
KV_evictions: 9123
KV_misses/sec: 230
mb_wait_us  p50 p95 p99
  120    340  880
kernel_choice_counts: A: 78% B: 22%
threads_blocked_on_eviction: 42
```
aj: thanks. also from CPU profiling: GC-like stalls around the eviction sweeper (not actual GC). kernel-A spends 34us per token, kernel-B 48us but kernel-B avoids the extra memcpy. so when evictions cause miss+rehydrate, kernel-A path gets penalized more.
sam: proposed mitigations: 1) lower microbatch target from 8 -> 4 when KV pressure > threshold; 2) prefer kernel-B when avg_kv_miss_rate > 0.05 (even for short seqs); 3) add non-blocking KV rehydrate path to avoid MB builder stall.
jia: quick A/B on canary: toggled kernel preference for a small pool. result: p99 reduced from ~560ms -> ~260ms at same throughput, but p50 increased slightly (120 -> 150). tradeoff looks acceptable for SLOs.
maria: good. any suggestions on telemetry knobs so customers can opt in?
aj: expose two flags: `mb_target_size` and `kv_safe_kernel` plus an auto mode that flips based on `kv_miss_rate` and `threads_blocked_on_eviction`. defaults: mb_target_size=6, kv_safe_kernel=auto.
sam: also add a hedged-request counter: if KV rehydrate latency > X ms, spawn speculative secondary kernel-B execution after Y ms to cut tail. needs careful tokens accounting.
jia: note: hedging increases compute cost; we should gate it by SLO profile (only for enterprise tenants with tail-SLOs).
maria: plan: 1) roll canary with kernel preference change + mb_target_size down on 10% of traffic; 2) add telemetry dashboard for kv_miss_rate + mb_wait_us; 3) open a follow-up for non-blocking rehydrate work.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/safe-kernel-rollout -> 10% @ 1865432120
aj: monitoring the canary now. will post p50/p99 snapshots in 10m.
maria: thanks all — great catch. will consolidate notes into perf playbook after we validate. :thumbsup:
